utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Before we invite you to continue, Mr. Russo, a few matters. First, the Chamber urges you to see how far you will come today. If you would need one day and two sessions, then certainly we couldn't finish this witness Monday, and that would then -- since we have on Tuesday, we have a videolink. That would mean that we would have to stay over. The Chamber is still exploring possibilities on sitting Monday morning as well but that's not yet final, and we'll see at the end of the day what is appropriate to give you as extra time. That also depends on how you use your time today. That is one issue. Another matter is that the Chamber has invited the Prosecution to reduce the size of the statements given by the accused. I think 1200 pages were tendered, and we couldn't imagine all 1200 were so relevant that we should keep all of them. But we haven't heard from the Prosecution since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes Mr. President. We are preparing a submission for the court regarding that. However, we did indicate in the motion that it was the 300 pages that we had selected was what we believed the Court should focus on; however, we did include the entire interview in fairness both to the accused and to all counsel. But I'm sure we can resolve that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question is when.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It's my understanding, Your Honour, that we filed last night and it will be distributed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will have a look at it. Thank you. Any other matter? Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just on that last point, Mr. President, we have -- the time is running on our response. Should -- will we get extra time to comment on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The selection --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- or on the admission of the statements as such?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll understand that if we wait to have the response and only then say we'd like to have at least the size reduced then, of course, that would take all together quite a bit of time. How much time would you need for a response?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The issue, Mr. President, is although they're not our statements we may have some comment on -- and there's been litigation about this in this Tribunal in the past, about comments from one person and how they impact against the co-accused. We would have to go through that transcript and then point out where we object. We can't do that until we see what the final product is going to be from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you are in a position to assess that. Does the issue of not being able to cross-examine on the statement where an accused who gave a statement is not called as a witness in his own case?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just put in short. I see your point. I could even imagine that you raise fundamental issues already and that you give further details at a later stage, but, just as I said to Mr. Russo, the "when" is important for the Chamber. Could you give us an estimate on when you think you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, at this point and based on the current filing we would try to get something filed by next Thursday which is, I think, the 14 days would expire then. If the Court wishes to proceed in the manner that we give the general position and if there is anything specific that we need to comment on after the Prosecution has made its selection, if the Court would indulge us by allowing us a brief submission on those points and that's how we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we could resolve that in a practical way. I suggest that we have communication through legal officer about what we expect when. Is that -- all parties agree with that. Thank you for that. Any other matter? Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, just one issue with regard to redirect and just efficient uses of time. I do have some standing in that regard given my expertise in the questioning about striped underwear or wearing it, I'm not sure. In any event, we're talking about the revisiting the 92 ter statement, Mr. President, I mean, let us be honest. The most efficient use of our time at this juncture is to operate with the 92 ter statement in front of the Chamber, in front of the witness. We inquired last night or yesterday afternoon as to the Prosecution's intentions concerning redirect on the 92 ter statement. I will tell you I have -- visually it's difficult to see, but the vast majority of this as I've underlined are areas that the Prosecution has said that they may cover during redirect examination. That will significantly protract the period of time that this witness will be here and before the Chamber. So ... Again, I represent -- given the testimony yesterday and how we have presented this, I submit to the Chamber that the most efficient way to do this is: Let's go back to the 92 ter statement and let's go embark from there, and then we can cut out or we can certainly limit the amount of time this witness is here. And certainly, you know, I would think that the Chamber needs, when you're gauging time, how much time the Prosecution intends to use during redirect because if it's yet another three hours, then that changes the dynamics of this dramatically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. I took from your estimate of perhaps 45 minutes, that you'd go through the 92 ter statement rather quickly, and, of course, the Chamber reads it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I can imagine but that's, I would say, a general experience that the party that cross-examines or the party that responds to evidence which was produced under 92 ter, usually takes far more time than the 92 ter statement itself takes. That's understood. And I can imagine that under those circumstances you would need a bit more time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I appreciate that Mr. President, but I don't know if the chamber has read the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think Your Honour would agree with me that many of the issues that we discussed over the past couple of days, we could have used the 92 ter statement as a jumping-off point to just get some clarity or some additional questions on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether or not that's the case, I do not express any opinion on that. I take it that Mr. Russo would consider his approach a better one than to start with the 92 ter. Mr. Russo, is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My position is the same with respect to the order, Mr. President. However, I should clarify, last night I was -- or yesterday --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please turn off all unnecessary microphones, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yesterday, I was asked by the Defence to indicate to them what portions of the 92 ter statement I believed fell outside of the scope of my direct. I did provide with them that information yesterday. However, I think there is a miscommunication with respect to what that meant. I was simply indicating to them the matters within the statement, I believed, fell outside of my direct examination but not that I was intending full cross-examination on all of those matters. I am not going to be going forever on redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, would you not be allowed to go forever. If there's any chance of miscommunication, perhaps communicate again during the next break. And let's then get started. Unless there is any other matter at this moment, Mr. Kehoe. The mere fact that the Chamber is exploring further time may be an indication already that the Chamber is aware that the way in which the testimony is presented of this witness might not be easily concluded in one session in one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge. And I will address with Mr. Russo what we believe in the 92 ter statement falls outside direct examination and possibly we can shave that down a bit, so we will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We should take care that not a discussion of -- on what is within and what is outside the scope of a certain matter takes more than the few questions that might be put in that respect. Mr. Kehoe, any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Russo, are you ready to continue your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, one small matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the Chamber is awaiting the remaining Turkalj submission. The -- we have agreed, Ms. Mahindaratne and I, on the revisions, and I'm just going to -- all I need to do is formalise the stipulations so we can get that to the Chamber, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rajcic. Mr. Rajcic, I would like to remind you that the some declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony still binds you. That may be clear to you. Mr. Russo will now continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Russo, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Good morning again, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness approach the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you come a bit closer to the microphone, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'd like to pick up today where we left off yesterday with your indicating targets in Knin that were fired upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could please have Exhibit P62.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I believe at the end of the day yesterday we left off with your indication of an area of cross-roads; although, you were uncertain as to which cross-roads specifically it was. I'd like to now move on from that --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: -- and ask you to please indicate, in addition to any of the targets that you've already circled in the town, if you could tell us what other targets in the town were actually fired at on 4 or 5 August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the corps artillery is concerned, the Tvik factory was fired at, as well as the Senjak barracks, Milan Martic's residence, and the already mentioned area around the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: You just mentioned the already mentioned area around the hospital. Were you referring to there the two circles that you indicated yesterday, or another location?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was referring to one of the two circles, not both.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now, the other places that you've indicated --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could please enlarge the image in the area where it says "Knin general supply," about the middle of the photograph. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, you indicated the -- the Senjak barracks. If can you see here, there is an area marked "Knin general supply." Does that area conform to the location -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. I -- based on what I can see from -- from this aerial image. But I would have to check the coordinates from the table of targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. And immediately to the right of that area marked "Knin general supply," is that the area, that factory complex, is that the area that you understand to be the Tvik factory?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That should be the factory complex called Tvik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And the final target you mentioned was Milan Martic's residence. Are you able to indicate for us where that residence is located?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hit, yeah. It was hit. I can't be certain. I could identify it by finding the police station, because I believe it was one of the housing blocks near the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, if we could move the photograph a little bit to the left -- I'm sorry, to the right. Little bit more. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, you marked for us yesterday, Mr. Rajcic, the area of the police station, which I believe is a bit below and to the left of the sign that indicates Knin general supply. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember, and I believe I showed this particular building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Are you able to tell, since you can recognise where the police station is, are you able to tell us the general area or the building, in fact, that you believed was Mr. Martic's residence?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I wouldn't like to speculate. I would have to see the coordinates from the table and then compare it to the map. I can see that there are several large residential blocks around the police station, and I never went to that flat personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine. We'll come back to that a bit later. So is there -- or were there any targets in addition to the ones that you've circled on this map and the ones that you've indicated here today, those being the Senjak barracks, the Tvik factory, and the residence of Milan Martic. Those three targets, plus the areas that you marked on the maps yesterday, anything else in the town of Knin that was fired at on 4 or 5 August, and I'm asking not just about the corps artillery but about any artillery of the Croatian forces on 4 or 5 August.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were other areas that were targeted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if you can tell us, please, what those areas were.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of the roundabout.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the last part of what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, the interpreters had difficulties in hearing exactly what you said. You were talking about a roundabout. Could you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to the roundabout area. In the course of combat activities, 130-millimetre cannons fired upon the places where, according to the intelligence received and electronic reconnaissance, Martic was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what area of town that was?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area around his flat and the area close to the railway station, that general swathe, so to speak. I would again have to look at the coordinates to be precise. I think that the area was called Stara Bolnica, old hospital, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And a bit earlier before you were asked to repeat your answer, you mentioned the area of the roundabout.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could please move the photograph a little bit down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Rajcic, do you see the roundabout you're talking about in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you please circle that and label it with an R.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm able to tell, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there, to your recollection, any other areas in Knin that were fired at about either corps artillery or any other artillery of the Croatian forces on 4 or 5 August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In downtown Knin, I think I marked all the relevant places or areas that were fired upon from 130-millimetre cannons of the corps artillery, and BM 21 launchers of 122-millimetres of the brigade missile weaponry as well as from 122-millimetre D-30 Howitzers. I believe it was the -- it was on the 5th of August that several rounds were fired by the 4th Guards Brigade from its -- or, rather, its artillery rocket battalion fired upon the Slavko Rodic barracks, or the northern barracks. Out in the periphery, to the best of my recollection, there was the bridge across the Butiznica river that we discussed yesterday, Mr. Russo, and you didn't show it to me on the image, and it was also targeted, as well as the intersection, or the cross-roads, of the periphery road leading to Cetinska, Dolina, and Vrlika. That's the extent of what I can tell you now without looking at the table of targets and the reconstruction I made.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could offer this into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, could we ask the witness whether the old hospital area could be marked on the map as well. Do you see, Mr. Rajcic, the -- I think you said the Stara Bolnica area on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As part of the final preparations, I did not deal with the old hospital area, and I might inadvertently show the wrong area. The area of the old hospital was a sudden target, which emerged in the course of combat and had not been planned. And you'll, I hope, understand if I do not mark it on this aerial image because I do not want to be imprecise and I would rather draw upon the Y, X, Z, coordinates, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then any objection against the marks tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2337 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, just going on what you just told His Honour, Judge Orie, you indicated that this area that was fired at, the area of the old hospital, "was a sudden target that emerged in the course of combat and had not been planned." I would like you to please tell us what it was about that, that required artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The flow of information coming from intelligence and electronic reconnaissance led us to learn that Milan Martic was in that area. I received the coordinates for the area, and, based on that, it was decided that several rounds should be fired at the area, and this is how it was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if could I ask the witness to take his headphones off, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, would you please take your earphones off for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just, I'm following him in the original, and there may be a different ways to translate the word he's using which may actually have quite a bit of relevance. He is use the word "prostor" in Croatian which can be translated as "area," but there is also a different translation, and in the context of artillery --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I take it that you will seek further explanation as to what he refers to if he says that several rounds were fired at "this area."

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That was my intention, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, I didn't hear the interpretation from the start, and I'd like to hear that so that I'm not missing out on something. And I'm referring to the moment when I put my headphones on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, you were the only one who spoke since you had your headphones on, so there should be no problem. Mr. Russo will put his next question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Martic -- sorry, Mr. Rajcic. Please forgive me for that. When you indicated that you received --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is human to make mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I appreciate that. You indicated that you had received intelligence that Mr. Martic was in a certain area. You were given coordinates for that area. When you describe it as an area, can you be specific for us and indicate whether it is a particular building, an area of town, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm speaking in general terms about an area. I'm not using artillery terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that. What I'd like to know is what you receive the coordinates for, and I understand that you can't be exactly precise. But are you able to tell us whether you were firing at a building you believed Mr. Martic to be in, or a particular section of town next to certain buildings that you believed him to be in?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, at the time the fighting was at its highest intensity, the intelligence body or official brings to the operations centre the data concerning a target in the form of X, Y, Z coordinates, and next to the coordinates, the word "Martic." To me, as an artillery officer, what matters at that point is whether this refers to a building or an open area, open space. I was told that it was a building, and we proceeded to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up, Mr. Rajcic. Now, are you able to tell us, if you can recall, at what time of the day it was that this happened? Was it very early in the morning, sometime in the afternoon, later in the evening, and on what day?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean which time of day or which particular date?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Both pieces of information, if you can provide it. And I'm asking you specifically about when you were given the X, Y, and Z coordinates in this area of the old hospital to fire on Mr. Martic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall it happening on the 4th of August. It was in the early evening, but I have to place a caveat there, because in August the sun sets shortly before 2100 hours; that's to say, 9.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. We're going to come back to this a bit later, but I'd like it move on for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, perhaps just one clarifying question. By that last observation, did you intend to say that it was still light, or that it was dark already when you received that information, or that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It was still day-time. But I said roughly late afternoon/early evening, because certain things, if mistaken, could easily lead to wrong conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'd like to move now to the reconstruction you did regarding what you describe as the second and third organisational levels of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could please have 65 ter 7067.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, Mr. Rajcic, I notice you don't have your binder with you today. Do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, if we could, please stay on the first page in the English version but go to the third page in the B/C/S version, although, Mr. Rajcic, I believe your first page is also the first page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please. Mr. Russo, I have the first page in the binder, where it says the analysis, not reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you check one of the other tabs?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recognise this as the -- your reconstruction that you did on the second and third levels of organisation for artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is for the first establishment level.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is it okay if I take his binder for a moment and find where it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give it back, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was assisted in finding this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you have got in front of you now what you see on your screen. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now have I it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My apologies to the court officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Is this the reconstruction that you drafted?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the second page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And for you, Mr. Rajcic, I believe that would be -- in the B/C/S would be page 4. And I'm looking at the last sentence of the second paragraph in the introduction.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the second page for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rajcic. My apologies for that. The problem is that in e-court we have two additional pages at the beginning which do not appear in your binder because they're just cover sheets, so when I call out the B/C/S page, I'm calling it out for the registrar and then you can deduct two pages from that to find it in your binder, and I'm simply going to give you the section as well, so you can find it by the section number, if that will work?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems to me that I heard it was the fourth page for me, or in my case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: My apologies for that. We're looking at the --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Errare humanum est" as I already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could look the last sentence of the second paragraph in the introduction, and there you state: "The artillery of the 4th Guards Brigade and the 7th Guards Brigade, we classify as minus third level. The method used in this review ensures the understanding of real use, role, and impact of artillery and rocket weapons of the 4th Guards Brigade and the 7th Guards Brigade in the Operation Storm (Kozjak 95). This reconstruction is not a supposition or estimate, but a review of the real event, which is corroborated by authentic documents produced before, during, and after the offensive operation. "There were neither modulations nor specific artillery organisation at the second level of command of the operations groups, OG." Now, Mr. Rajcic, can you please explain these two organisational levels that you refer to, the second and the third, and explain how they relate to the corps artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before that, I would like to say that the interpretation was incorrect. It concerns the bold section in the text, which says at the second level of commander of the operations group, there was no modulating or purpose organisation of artillery, and not the second level of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you please explain to us what you mean when you said that at the second level of command of the operations there was no modulating or purpose organisation of artillery? What does that exactly mean, in layman's terms, if you could?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When one organises all actors in one operations group or in all operation groups or in other forms of organising troops of purposeful or special purpose organising, since operations groups are also special purpose organisations they're not establishment units. Following from that, all organic parts of operations groups -- or, rather, brigades, regiments, or independent battalions, they all have in their establishment, they also have artillery. If we put into a system of subordination, the relationship between the command of the Military District and the operations group, then operations group in terms of its level, the first subordinated formation, so it's first subordinated to the commander of the Military District. In other words, in my reconstruction, I marked that as the second level. The first level would be the command of the Military District. In the time immediately preceding Operation Storm, when the activities are the most intensive and the pace is the quickest, after commander's order, the main commander's order, on the way and model of the carrying out of the operation on organizing the overall resources --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'm sorry, I don't mean to cut you off but we're a bit limited in time. I do understand from your answer that this second level was a level immediately below the Military District --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: -- and that it did not have its own specific artillery groups, if that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had their own artillery, but they didn't modulate of special purposes organisations of artillery so that operations groups commanders could have, so to speak, executive and discretionary right to direct such artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And that being in contrast to what was done at the corps level. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's different. It doesn't have to be contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, that's perhaps a better designation. It was not the same type of organisational artillery as existed at the corps level. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's different organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could move to section 3.1.1, which appears on page 3 in the English version, and page 5 of B/C/S on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, that may appear on page 3 of your version. That's section 3.1.1. In this section, you indicate the activities of the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The activities of the 7th Guards Brigade in the artillery preparation on 4 August 1995. You indicate that they fired from 122-millimetre self-propelled rocket launchers, 112 rockets at three targets in Knin, according to the map, Ivancica. The first target you mention is S15 which you do not specifically identify. The second is S16, which you identify as the Slavko Rodic barracks. And the third target is S54, which you identify as the command post and communications centre. Do I have that correct, Mr. Rajcic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a bit unclear to me. I'm not sure whether it was clear to you. Your Honours, if you allow me before answering, I would comment this material, if allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could briefly do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the final version of my reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did you draft another version and provide it to the government of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last version, the consolidated version of this material, which did not contain typos, as far as I could notice, there are some other details which do not correlate. I rectify those in the final version, and apart from that, work on the -- producing this reconstruction was a process characterized by regular influx of new materials, reports, or new information from the preparational executive part of the operation. I'll try to recall the date. In January this year, I think it was the 28th or the 29th of January, I signed the final draft of that reconstruction, and I still believe that the final draft itself is not final or complete. That was left with the criminal investigation department of the Zagreb police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And other than the criminal investigation department of the Zagreb police, did you give a copy of that final reconstruction draft -- final version of the reconstruction to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, I do not deliver. The government was my employer; I used to work for the government. And the material that I prepared, not as it stands here but in the version that I prepared, with respect to that, I did not have the right to distribute that to anybody and I signed official secret statement in the minister of defence's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if there's anything that I ask you about here in the report that you changed between this version in front of you and your final version, please let us know that. You indicated there were some typos and other materials which did not correlate. If we touch upon any of those in my questions, if you would please point those out to us. But for now, I want to concentrate on this area, section 3.1.1 and the three targets that that you mentioned there S15, S16, and S54? Is that correct, Mr. Rajcic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the S15, S16, and S54 are marks for the targets, the code map Ivancica used by the 7th Guards Brigade. Here I would like to ask Their Honours if I were to be given some homework for the break, to go through this version because this is not the final version. I waive my right to a break so that can I go through this version and do my homework.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't often happen that it's offered spontaneously, Mr. Rajcic. If you would --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of clarity, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we gladly accept your offer to go through this version. Not to say that we haven't -- at least, Mr. Russo, I take it you don't have later versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: We were not provided with a later version, Mr. President. However, I would simply request that if the witness is going to do us the favour of going through this reconstruction that he do so in writing and simply write down what he thinks needs to be changed so that we don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, it would be even better to have, on an urgent basis, the new version. That avoids all kind of -- if there is any way to get it -- otherwise, it's appreciated, Mr. Rajcic, if would you read through it. If it's just a matter of five or six corrections, then, first the thing is to establish where and what kind of corrections are needed, and then we'll see whether we'll make them in court or whether there will be any other way of -- of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I cannot do so without basic documentation, which was used to generate this reconstruction. I cannot find any radical differences. I don't have the processing or memory capacity in my brain to memorise all of these. I noticed one detail here, which doesn't seem correct to me, although it goes for a work -- working version, which is not a final, but acting in good faith, and to prevent misinformation to be published, I'm willing, in order to do so, to go through this material during the break and rectify it, wherever possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, if this takes one or two days in court, then it doesn't make much sense to do it. Then, of course, we'd invite to you write it down in one way or another or to perhaps someone to assist you in dictating what is wrong so that we have a -- the most recent information. But I've got no idea about how much work that would be. Whenever Mr. Russo asks you questions, and if you're uncertain as to whether the questions are related to parts of the report that might not be the most accurate version, please, indicate that so that we can then move on and limit ourselves at this moment to what is not in dispute. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, again, the targets that you've indicated in section 3.1.1, that is target S15, S16, which you identify as the Slavko Rodic barracks, and the third target, S54, which you identify as the command post and communication centre. Were those targets actually fired at by the 7th Guards Brigade, with 122-millimetre rockets on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They open fire at S15, S16 and S54. I repeat, I remember in my work having insight into the documentation of the 7th Guards Brigade, which was at my disposal, there were some doubts as to the target S16, in terms of the presentation of the target. I remember a personal diary of a lower-ranked commander, I think it was the calculator's diary. And this is why I put in parenthesis in this working version, Slavko Rodic barracks. As far as I can recall what stood there to the right of S16. And for that to be precisely reconstructed, I had to put myself in the shoes of that person, who, at that time, indicated the target, and we will all agree this is tantamount to science fiction. True, those dilemmas where the areas where I exhausted myself fully. I did, however, use that as an anchor, the coded map Ivancica, and in the aforementioned diary, it states the S16 target, which still has not sunk in, in my own mind. Therefore, I cannot claim with 100 percent certainty that this was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think we need a correction on the transcript line 25. Yes, S16. Let's have a look at the Ivancica map, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to call this exhibit up. However, I was instructed to advise the Court when it is one of the documents that is not on the 65 ter list. This is annex 12 to the particular reconstruction that we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was not on the 65 ter list. When did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: We received it on the 10th of October, 2008.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against adding this document to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The stated objections we raised previously, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was an annex to a report which was on the 65 ter list, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: This is an annex to the report which we -- which is already in evidence, P2326.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber grants leave to add it to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could please have 65 ter 6124.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, do you recognise this as the coded map, Ivancica?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is stated so, coded map, Ivancica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could focus on the area to the north-west of the S, of the large S in bold, right there. I'm going to ask that that be significantly enlarged. A bit more. That's fine. Thank you. Now, Mr. Rajcic, you can see the target area, 16. It's the second one immediately above the word "Knin" on the map. Do you see it there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, northwards, above the word "Knin." I can see it. To the left 13; to the right 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, thank you for describing that. Now, the target area, 16, you can see that it covers a little bit of main road there in red and then covers the area to the east of the main road. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, the Slavko Rodic barracks is actually west of that main road, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To the north-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Meaning a bit north and west of the position of -- the target area S16?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These maps were made, as far as I know, with the final modifications in 1996 or 1998. The former JNA did not plot its installations into military maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell me why the 7th Guards Brigade would be firing on the target area 16, with multiple-barrel rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, the diary that I read and I believe you have within the material you received, reads to the right of S16. And I'm not referring to my material. I'm referring to the material taken out of the archive or obtained in another manner. This material that I made was not made for your purposes but for the purpose of the government of the Republic of Croatia, and this is something I brought to the attention of the representatives of the government. As far as S16 is concerned, if you look at it in my reconstruction and if you seem puzzled by what you see in brackets, S. Rodic barracks, let me tell you that, based on the indicated target, I - this is to the right of S16 - I subjectively identified the barracks in that particular sector. I do urge you to look at that diary at some point, because I used it to precisely define the location where rockets were supposed to land.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I just want to make sure I understand you --

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. Russo, I have to make this observation, and if I'm mistaken, please correct me. When you look at the map as it stands, what is on the right-hand side seems in a different way to us than as it appeared to the commander who issued the order to attack. He had a different perspective of it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not certain if you're mistaken about that, Mr. Rajcic. I don't know that I can speak to that. But I would like you to explain what that means. First of all, the commander who issued the order to attack, can you tell me who it is exactly you're referring to there, and what perspective he had of this map?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Always where artillery is used, before, during, and later, through different techniques of use an operation of -- and direction of artillery fire, left, right, proximal, distal, this is something that refers to the trajectory of the shell, or a rocket, a missile. When a commander decides -- we're speaking in hypothetical terms. Where a commander decides to prepare for an artillery attack and where it's been decided that as part of preparations for the artillery attack, an attack should be launched to the right of S16, then it is the task of all those who are part of the chain of command to recognise and understand what it is all about. Standard operative procedures and methods of work relating to the way in which the target is indicated, the way in which the coordinates are taken, unless they're there, in my personal view, in this particular instance there were no X/Y coordinates. Rather, a coded map was used to indicate the target and quite legitimately so. In answer to your question then, the lowest rank -- the lowest ranking or lowest level officer knows that along his axis of attack this is to the right of S16, and he will enter into this area of the Slavko Rodic barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, where you indicate -- I understand your explanation with respect to S16, and we're going to go back to your reconstruction about that. I do understand it now, as it relates to another section I wanted to ask you about. But for now, since we have the map in front of us, the targets S15 and S54 that were also indicated as targets in section 3.1.1 of your reconstruction, were those targets fired at or are we also now talking about firing to a different angle of those?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are not talking about anything different here. As an artillery man myself, so to speak, when I visualise plastically, the area where the multiple rocket launchers were positioned in the Grahovo area, and when I find my bearings, which I believe I'm quite good at, then the target S15 is merely the continuation of that direction, of course if it is within range; whereas, target S54 has a deviation from that central line of fire, or trajectory, in relation to the other two targets. It's a deflection to the left, the vantage point being the direction of fire by some two to three degrees, approximately speaking, of course. There is a technique employed to measure the deflection, and there are instruments to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I do appreciate that explanation, Mr. Rajcic. I just want a very simple answer, if you can give me one; and if you can't, please let me know. Did the 7th Guards Brigade fire multiple-barrel rocket launchers on the target S15 and S54, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said at the start, when we started analysing 3.1.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. Referring to what had you already written in section 3.1.1, that is correct. Am I right about that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would offer 65 ter 6124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That being admitted to the 65 ter list. Are there any objections against admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, the objection still remains the same, whether it was added to the list or not, about late disclosure, about the prejudice to the Defence, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It will be MFI'd and the Chamber will decide later.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2338, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Russo. Although we are close to a moment when we usually have a break. If you want to start on a new subject ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm going to stay on this subject, Your Honour, but it's probably a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a break, and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to inform the parties that the Chamber has booked Monday morning, in addition to the existing schedule. Whether we need it or not, we'll know at the end of today's session. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could please go to 65 ter 7067.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And this is, again, your 4th and 7th Guards Brigade reconstruction, Mr. Rajcic. And I'd like to focus on section 4.1.1. This appears in the English version on page 12, and in B/C/S, in e-court, on page 11. Now, if we go to the bottom of the page in English, and I wanted to ask you about this, Mr. Rajcic, which I think correlates to what you were explaining to us earlier, with respect to the target that we looked at on the Ivancica map. In the third paragraph there of that section -- are you with me on section 4.1.1?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, in the third paragraph it indicates that the 4th Guards Brigade fired rockets on the 4th of August at the Slavko Rodic barracks in the town of Knin, and here you say: "Between S13, S16, S17 and S21, coded map, Ivancica, the unit spent 89 rockets." Is that what you were explaining to us earlier that what appeared between those target circles is what was actually fired at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that should be it. I would have to have the map Ivancica on the screen, though, because from the four positions, the target which is fired at, is being located.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move a few pages back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, if we can go to section 3.2.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And at the bottom of the page in English, that's page 4 in the English, I wanted to ask you about the timing in this paragraph, Mr. Rajcic. It indicates that the 7th Guards Brigade -- indicates that the 7th Guards Brigade on the 5th of August, fired 40 rockets at target S54 on the Ivancica map at 0400 hours and 40 rockets at the Slavko Rodic barracks at 0500 hours. I wanted to ask you specifically about the times. Is the time of 0400 hours correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the document that I had at my disposal, that appears to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move now to section 3.3.1 which appears in the English on e-court on page 5. And this covers -- it's under the section for covering 6th August 1995. However, it indicates there in the second paragraph that there was a 152-millimetre Howitzer was seized in the town of Knin on the 5th of August. Now, there's no citation of attachments for that particular section. I'd like to ask you what you -- what you base that on, the seizure of that piece of artillery in the town of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was working on this document, I had a request to make of the minister of defence. Specifically, I wanted him to give me his approval to talk with the active officer, Brigadier Zdravko Jakov who, at the time, the position of chief of artillery of the 7th Guards Brigade. From my conversation with him and to the best of my recollection, I knew that the 7th Guards Brigade, on their arrival in Knin, on the way into town, found a 122-millimetre [as interpreted] D-20 Howitzer, which was left behind. The forces seized the artillery piece, and together with the other assets belonging to the same brigade, everything was transferred to the area of Grahovo, in order to provide reinforcements and reinforce that -- the right flank of our forces in the direction of Drvar and Grahovo. Brigadier Jakov confirmed this to me verbally. For that reason, in relation to the 6th of August, I indicated this as one of the methods of work I employed while I was working on this reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think we may need a correction on line 12 of page 33. Did you indicate, Mr. Rajcic, that it was a 122-millimetre or a 152-millimetre D-20 Howitzer?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 152 D-20. If I misspoke, then I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. In and in speaking with brigadier Zdravko Jakov regarding the seizure of this piece of artillery, did you gain any information as to, first of all, the exact location where it was found, and, second of all, whether it was dug in, in position, or simply abandoned on the road? Can you give us any information with respect to that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was abandoned on the road. In the area called Kovacic, Kovacic is the toponym covering several neighbourhoods in the periphery of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to move into evidence 65 ter 7067.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. My understanding is this -- this was not one of the ones that was initially presented. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It is one of the ones in the motion to add Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And -- with this particular report?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your report to us has it italicised as just the opposite, but I just take your word for it. If it's part of that initial motion was made to you -- to the Court, then we have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since there seems to be disagreement the Chamber will admit the exhibit into evidence, but on the basis of information -- of the information provided by Mr. Russo. If that information turns out not to be correct, the Chamber would like to be informed and then we will reconsider which is not the same as not to admit, but then we will reconsider on the basis of the correct information, whether it should be admitted, yes, or not -- yes or no. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will become Exhibit P2339.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, you created another corps level reconstruction which is similar in many ways to the 1st Corps level reconstruction that we looked at earlier. I'd like to take a look at that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 7064.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I had -- and did my homework during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that causes you to tell us what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we discussed the document about -- and the working material about the second and third establishment level, paragraph 3, 3.1.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: The section being referred to is on --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 3 in my version.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: It also begins at the bottom of page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 3.1.2, artillery support to attack, the words "used 151 rockets," that would be paragraph 1 of that subsection, item, or paragraph, whichever term you use. As far as I can recall, this is an mistake stated here which was subsequently corrected. I think -- I think it was 70 to 80 rockets which later has implications for the paragraph 3.1.3, total spent ammunition on the day, 4th of August, 1995, by the artillery of the 7th Brigade. Rockets, 122-millimetre, 9M22U to 63, as quantity is not stated, but the value should be lower. utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have -- Well, first, Mr. President, this attachment is not on the 65 ter list.

utterances.text: Basically the same objection, Your Honour. We admitted back in February four documents, the 65 ter, because they were limited documents not considering all these attachments. utterances.text: I drafted this because, apart from the documents that were available from the artillery groups 3 and 4, to prepare a more quality reconstruction. And some parts of the war diary of the Sector 1 which, according to the information contained therein, was in the area of Stari Grad, Seline, Maslenica. The purpose of this attachment was also to confirm, on the basis of those documents, and to establish correlations in the system of command and control over artillery and rocket groups and artillery groups. Here we defined them as being of the first level, meaning corps artillery, and to express the relationship of subordination between the chief commander and subordinated units, and the coordination in horizontal sense, at the horizontal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And there in those two entries we can see above where the actual entry in the diary is; for example, in 0555 hour it indicates chief of artillery orders TS 2 that 203 guns should open fire against Drnis. And below that you have interlineated: TS-2, and in parenthesis you put TS-4, did not care out this order because the OG chief of artillery was not authorised to command TS-4. At that time 0550 hours, TS-4 fired two rounds from a Howitzer, 230-millimetre gun at the repeater on Promina and you make a similar comment with respect to the entry at 0625 hours. utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an equal understanding of the Artillery Group 2, and Artillery Group 4, respectively. And I think that on the first day I said that before Operation Storm, training was conducted and preparations were conducted for possible attacks. That was a period preceding the time when Croatian forces launched attack beyond the Dinara mountain, along the Drvar-Grahovo axis. That documentation, before that time, was prepared in the Sibenik Operations Group, which existed in terms of organisation and operations before that time, and plan documents were put in an envelope and, according to those plans, Artillery Group 2 was referred to there. And the artillery group after the action on the Dinara mountain, at the time when the decision had not yet been taken for the forces of the Croatian Defence Council to be co-opted among the forces of the Croatian army for Operation Storm, and for that reason we have those changes; whereby, looking from right to left, Artillery Group 1 becomes Artillery Group 3; Artillery Group 2 becomes Artillery Group 4; and the Artillery Group 3 becomes artillery rocket group. And for that reason, during the first stages of the attack, the chief of artillery of the Sibenik Artillery Group suffered from a misunderstanding, in terms of the numbers being attached to certain groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO

utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.text: That's a code-name for the commander of TS-3. Excuse me, and for the 130 cannon unit.

utterances.text: Thank you for clearing that up. Now, how can you tell from looking at this entry -- or can you tell from looking at this entry, or for any of the entries in 4 August in this diary, what it was exactly that was fired at 0500 hours?

utterances.text: And the tables of targets that you referred to as what you had at your disposal, are those the target lists that we've looked at here in court?

Combat is a different matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That last document that you mentioned, the list that you prepared yourself and that the units of TS-3 and TS-4 had, I don't find that list in your attachments to this document. Is that correct? Did you attach that particular document to this reconstruction?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have it at the time I was making the reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Have you subsequently seen that document?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us when the last time you saw that particular target list was?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I think it was in 1996, in the month of December, when General Ante Gotovina ordered, and an organisational order was written to gather the war material for all the operations carried out by the Split Military District and the operations jointly carried out with the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for explaining that, Mr. Rajcic. Can you give us any information, first of all, as to how many projectiles were fired at each salvo?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Every three minutes salvos at Drvar and Knin," if I can make this out. Calculations have to be made, this has to be analysed and compared. When the unit after this particular combat task set out to deal with other situations, newly arisen situations, or new targets, we would have to look into all that. Otherwise, I can't give you a specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you know why -- or what the purpose was of firing every three minutes? Is there a purpose behind that particular pattern?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your answer. It seems to indicate "I know." Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know. I know why.

utterances.text: Please tell us, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may take some time, though. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you would first give us the short answer. If we then need further details, we'll ask you for those details. So if you could give us a brief answer, to start with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a typical combat action, which has the purpose of disturbing, distressing the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rajcic, for that brief answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, at this time I would move for the admission of 65 ter 7060.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's the same objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document will be marked for identification. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could I ask one or two further details on the salvos. The salvos, what were you firing, in order to achieve this result, disturbing, distressing the enemy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were firing shells from 130-millimetre cannon. There were two cannons because the salvo includes two projectiles every three minutes on specific targets, and I believe that, time-wise, it lasted one hour. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is anything more known about the targets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all the available information about the targets must be gathered. I spoke about the tactical and technical characteristics of a target on the first day of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. But if you fire at a target 20 times in one hour, what would be, apart from disturbing the enemy, or distressing him, what would be the military advantage, as far as the target itself is concerned? The structure, the area, the -- whatever the target may have been.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, destroying as one of the combat actions cannot be included into this one. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this way, a military advantage can be gained.
