utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could go back to the first entry that we looked at, at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I just want to ask you one question about one of the entries there. It indicates at the second line: "Following the artillery preparation, the MiG 21 aircraft bombed the radio relay station Celavac very efficiently." Now, can you tell the Chamber, first of all, why the Celavac radio relay station was bombed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the radio relay hub, or node. It's one of the main systems used by the army of the so-called Republic of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you identify for us what the other main radio relay stations were?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to our area of responsibility, the link with Celavac was the radio relay Cumina [phoen] or the repeater at Promina. That was in the area where the enemy was deployed. As far as the area where we were deployed, there is one at Labisnica, then to the south toward at Dubrovnik at Sveti Ilija. Further on, on Peljesac and deep behind Dubrovnik, there was one location, Molunat where there was a radar station as well; and all of the latter fell within our area of deployment. Excuse me, this is the infrastructure of the radio communications system, which was installed in the former Yugoslavia and which was predominantly used by the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And those radio relay stations and repeaters that you have mentioned, were all of those attacked with aircraft or with a combination of aircraft and artillery or by some other means?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, all of those that I listed are the overall system of communications in the area from the Mount Velebit to Dubrovnik. Only two of those relay nodes or relay hubs, the Celavac node and Promina, were used by the enemy, the adversary. Those two relay nodes were the target of attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Now, I'd like to move back to your reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's P2336. Sorry, I think I neglected to offer 65 ter 397 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Registrar, could you assign a number marking it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will become Exhibit P2344, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: At your original reconstruction, P2336, that's the first document in your binder, I'd like to go to section 5.8.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, before we do that if I may just interrupt, and if can I ask the witness to take the headphones off because I don't want to make an objection without that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, could you please take off your earphones. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as we're on P2336, and we have been talking about page 10 as well as the -- going through the sources of information that were in P2336, starting from page 10 going up to page 11 in the English, and we have been dancing around the issue as to whether or not these -- these entities fired without authorisation -- fired on targets without authorisation, and it's incumbent upon the Prosecution to put that -- put their case to the witness, not dance around this issue. Put the case to the witness and ask him the questions based on what they just went through: Did they fire on authorisation, and did they fire on targets that were not predesignated targets pursuant to an X, Y, Z coordinates and a tabular textual table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a direct examination. The requirement to put a case to a witness is under Rule 90(H) which applies to cross-examination. The witness cited these four documents as the basis for indicating what was fired at. We took a look at those documents. That's the point I wanted to make. If Mr. Kehoe wants to make another point, he is free to do it during cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, then invite the Chamber to do it. The issue here through this point being made by the Prosecution is that there was some type of unauthorised fire that was done not pursuant to predesignated targets. Now, if in fact the Prosecution wants to find out what this witness has to say about that and what the bottom line is, they should be asking that question. They certainly can take him through the documents as they have done, but what is the bottom line? The bottom line is that question which they fail to ask. They're the Prosecution. They should be putting their case to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If I could just respond briefly, Your Honour. First of all, I'm not going to argue my case right now. I'm certainly not going to argue it with the witness. The evidence is what I'm interested in at this point. The inference is that we wish to draw arguments we wish to make based on the evidence, do not necessarily conform to what Mr. Kehoe is putting to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, Rule 90(H) specifically mentions the duty to a cross-examining party to put its case to a witness. A similar rule certainly is not to be found in any other rule. Any legal authority for this application?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I agree that the rule itself obligates the Defence to do that or anybody that's engaged in cross-examination; however, I would in this particular point at this particular trial, I believe that in the interests of justice which puts the Prosection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, no. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you whether there was any legal authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I will give you the legal authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The legal authority is that Your Honour can craft and make rulings in the interest of justice as Your Honour and the Chamber has done throughout this. Certainly, this falls into that category which is a penumbra of rights and privileges that the Chamber has and can so exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, since you're inviting us to go into areas where we have no written, legal authorities, the Chamber would prefer to have an early break. And we will resume at a quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Kehoe, you invited the Chamber to give certain instructions to Mr. Russo. The Chamber has considered your request and finds no basis for such an instruction in the Rules, and, further, considers that the interests of justice do not require to give such an instruction to Mr. Russo. Therefore, Mr. Russo is free to proceed as he wishes in that respect. There's another matter, Mr. Mikulicic, and I'm addressing you. The Chamber will issue a written decision on your request to be present at the other side of the line in a videolink, and already for practical purposes, I inform you that that decision will be -- will deny your request.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: All I can say, that I'm -- that I'm not happy with it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. If you ask for something, just without giving full reasons, it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I see the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is in line with the guidance as we find it one of the early Tadic decisions, so it's -- but you'll find the exact reasons in the decision which is important enough [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: So I'm exceptionally denied to be present at a -- exceptional circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, Mr. Mikulicic, you'll find all the reasons whether what is exceptional or not and what is an exception to an exception, wait until you have seen the decision. We just gave you already this decision in order to accommodate you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, I'd like to return to the issue of the targeting of Mr. -- Mile Martic, which we had talked about a little bit earlier this morning. First, I want to be -- I'd like you to clarify for us whether you were targeting Mr. Martic himself or you were targeting the building that he happened to be living in?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His flat in the building that he was living in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I do understand that. However, I'm trying to get at the distinction of what it was you were attempting to achieve. If he wasn't in the flat would you still be shelling the flat?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd like to show you one of the target lists that we've been looking at, the one you indicated that you had drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could have P1271.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And focussing on target KV 610, which is a little bit below what we see here, the designation of that target is apartment building complex. Are you able to tell us whether this building is the building that you believed Mr. Martic -- to be living in?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could now have Exhibit D1261. And if we could, please, focus on the target KV 610, which appears -- there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, do you agree that this represents the location in Knin of the quarters of Mr. Martic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree whether this facility was the one where Mr. Milan Martic resided. I have the coordinates, and the coordinates were solely relevant for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that. And just to advise you, this is what has been agreed between the parties, relatively speaking, as to where the target coordinates for KV 610 actually fall in Knin. Now, you mentioned earlier that you would need to see the area of the police station, because you believe it was close to that. I can tell thought circle which appears directly above KV 610, if you can see that, that is a circle of the location of the plotted coordinates of the police station. So looking at that, relative to looking at the cross where KV 610 falls, can you tell me if you generally agree that this is the layout of how close or how far away the quarters of Milan Martic were from the police station?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that this was close, this is relatively close. Relativity is what I spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If we could please have -- well, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, have you -- are you personally familiar with the building in which Mr. Martic lives? Have you ever seen the building where he lived?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never, until that point. Until the time it was targeted. Later, I had no interest in seeing where he lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when you saw it, are we talking about seeing it on a map or did you actually see the building in Knin itself?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood your question about seeing as whether I know the building, whether I had been in it before, during or after the operation. This is how I understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, my question is not necessarily whether you have been inside the building but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, apparently you want to know whether the witness ever personally observed the building which was believed to be the building in which Mr. Martic lived. Did you ever see that with your own eyes; that is, not on a photograph, not on a list, but just look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, can you first tell us -- well, you've never seen the building. What sources of intelligence did you have to indicate the location of Mr. Martic's flat?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Intelligence sources were processed and collected in the Military District's intelligence bodies. As far as I know, the collection of intelligence from such sources went through aerial photography, taken by pilotless drones. I think that also cadastral plans for that area were available, so documents which were not typically of military origin. I presume - I'm not sure - that there was word of mouth, somebody who had lived in that area, imparted information. That's one of the ways to collect information. Then visual. Visually there was no clear line of sight of the settlement of Knin before the operation started. I presume that intelligence officers determined the coordinates, X/Y, on of the basis of information and intelligence gathered in the way that I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, it is an apartment building complex. Do you know how many flats were in that building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know how many people were living in that building besides Mr. Martic himself?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Do you know by any chance how many storeys high the building is?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only presume.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, can you explain for us what you believed your chances were of actually injuring or killing Mr. Martic by firing artillery at his building?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very slight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And "very slight." Using artillery, can you tell us what were your chances of -- in any given situation firing artillery either from the 130-millimetre guns or from the 122-millimetre rocket systems, firing with either one of those weapons -- you're indicating no. Is there one of those weapon systems was not used?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 130-millimetre cannon. Only the 130-millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand, that when you were targeting Mr. Martic himself, it was only with this 130-millimetre gun.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, could you come a bit closer to the microphone. Interpreters have difficulties in hearing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I tend to come too close and then too far away. I haven't found the optimum spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now we discussed at the beginning of your testimony somewhat the relative inaccuracy of artillery weapons, and the fact that when artillery is fired at a particular building, it is inevitable that some projectile also not actually hit the building but will in fact fall next to it. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And I think you indicated earlier that there were other parts in the town, other areas in the town that you fired at; for example, this old hospital building because you believed Mr. Martic to be in there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Pursuant to intelligence sources and electronic surveillance, this is the information that was given to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And when you indicated that your chances of actually killing or injuring Mr. Martic by firing artillery at his building, if you knew those chances were very slight, can you tell us why it is you, nevertheless, decided to employ artillery in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goal was to make the main commander of the adversary insecure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Was there any goal other than making him insecure by use of artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a possible goal by using artillery and analysing its impact, and, if possible, if results would have been the killing of Mile Martic by shelling, that would have given us a significant military advantage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to -- I don't know if this microphone is working.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's working.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to show Exhibit P1265 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one other question. Mr. Rajcic, you mentioned electronic surveillance as one of your sources of knowledge. Was that attached to the person, attached to a vehicle? How do I have to -- was it a kind of a GPS-oriented system? I don't need a full explanation but just to better understand what "electronic surveillance" would have meant here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a platoon for electronic action. They had the necessary equipment. They eavesdrop on the electronic communications of the enemy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So electronic surveillance was mainly trying to overhear any electronic communication rather than a system by which you could spot where exactly a vehicle was or by a GPS system. That was not in place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this was no such equipment, only on the basis of radio communications, intercepted, and listening in on telephone conversation and the reactions contained therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for assisting me in understanding what "electronic surveillance" means in this context. Please proceed, Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: First taking one last look at the target plotting for KV 610 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to bring up on Sanction Exhibit P1265.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Rajcic, you can see, this is a representation of Knin taken from the aerial map, the aerial photograph which you've previously marked, and this is an interactive function, and I'm going to be attempting to go direct to the area where KV 610 falls. First I need to focus in. Now that's the Senjak facility which you have already pointed out, and looking at the -- this area here that I'm indicating, there is -- can you see a line of buildings which are a bit staggered from one another. And next to that, three large apartment complexes. And it's in this area here that --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Judge, I object this. I mean, this -- he can't lead -- go into this and start telling him. It's up to the witness to say what is [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what Mr. Russo is going to tell him. But, Mr. Russo, of course, if you were asking whether you see some trees there is or -- that's -- but if it is any sensitive information, which would lead the witness to the answers of the questions you put to him, that's, of course, not what are you expected to do in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. President. I'm just asking the witness to take a look at that, the layout of this, so that he can relate it to the next image that I'm going to show him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Rajcic, focussing on this line of buildings here that are somewhat scattered, we can use that as a reference point for what appears next to it. And what we're looking at here is a picture of a view taken from the Knin fortress, and I'd like to focus on that area. Now, the image is a bit blurry. But I do have a more finer image. But I want you to notice here that same line of buildings that's a bit staggered. And next to it, you can see there are several apartment complexes; one here, one behind it, and several others. Now, looking at this, can you say whether or not this is the area which is plotted as KV 610 and the area that you knew Mr. Martic's quarters to be in?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine. Now, Mr. Rajcic, given that you were targeting only Mr. Martic and not the building that he was living in, can you explain to us what consideration was given in the decision to use artillery on that building, or at him, while he's in that building, can you explain to us what consideration was given for the civilians who were also in that building on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rules of use of artillery ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm not certain I understand your answer. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, it also presupposes that were there civilians in that building at that time, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with you that that is included in the question, in that respect it's leading. Mr. Russo, I think the right way of putting the question is: Can you explain what consideration was given to the civilians that may have been present in those buildings at the time. Could you explain your reference to the rules of use of artillery. What do they teach us, exactly, in terms of attacking a building in order to hit a person, which is supposed to live in one of the apartment blocks in relation to others that may live in that same apartment block, and which were not targeted but may have been civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We took into consideration the rule of distinction, or apparent difference in, and the rule of proportionality. In Croatian we say "uravno tejo nostvo" [phoen], balancing out, because it is a non-disputable fact that in such a context civilians can also be found. If necessary, I can expound on this explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to Mr. Russo whether he needs -- he is seeking further clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think your answer is clear, Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask you a couple of more questions about the planning that went into the use of artillery for Operation Storm. I know we've discussed in some detail the planning for Knin. I wanted to focus a little bit more on the planning for Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac. You already indicated to us that at some point you developed a plan for artillery use in those three towns; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To certain delimitations, as opposed or as different from in the case of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell us when exactly it was that you began planning for the use of artillery, as an offensive operation, for the use of artillery against targets in those three towns?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day, when we discussed the target table for Knin, I said that this was a continuous process of processing the state of affairs on the battlefield when I discussed the target list after the incident in Biograd when our civilians and our soldiers were killed on the beach. The process of preparing the targets is a continuous process.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand the process, Mr. Rajcic, what I'm trying to determine is when the process began, in terms of finding targets in Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac that you may want to consider for artillery fire for an offensive operation.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the facilities which bore the character of military targets in those settlements - and I'm not going to list all of them - when I came in 1993 from the area of Dubrovnik into the command of General Gotovina, as early as then we defined such military facilities and determined the coordinates for them. And except for this part which does not have a category of military facility, they, later on, were just supplemented, until the eve of the operation -- of the attack, Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. And I understand that that's -- 1993 is when you came under the command of General Gotovina. That's when you picked -- or some of the targets in those towns, you located them. Can you tell us now when the decision was made to go ahead and actually use artillery against the targets in Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the activity status on the drafting of the order for attack of Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And that was when, time-frame?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, my contribution to that plan bears the date of 2nd of August, and on the 1st of August, we made the necessary analyses for the selection of targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to talk now a little bit about your knowledge of the command relationship that General Gotovina had with his subordinates. Let me first focus on the General. Can you tell, give the Chamber some idea of what kind of a commander General Gotovina was. Was he a strong commander, a weak commander? Can you explain some of that to us?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My impression of General Gotovina is that he was a top-notch professional, strict -- and a strict and just commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Did the officers and troops under General Gotovina's command respect him?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my knowledge, they held him in a high esteem and had great respect for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And as far as you're aware, were General Gotovina's orders always followed?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very dangerous not to comply with an order from General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with respect to Operation Storm in particular, was General Gotovina the highest operational commander in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? Operation Storm is an operation covering the entire area except for Slavonia. Are you referring only to Sector South?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm referring to the entire Operation Storm. Who was the highest operational commander in that operation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the military structure and subordination and the system of the Croatian army, that was the chief of the Main Staff for this particular operation, and in combat of such a level, it is the president of the state who is the chief commander. According to the Law on Defence of the Republic of Croatia, according to the Law on the Armed Forces, in war operation it is the president of the state who is the Commander-in-Chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that President Tudjman was the Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces. What I'm attempting to discover is -- I'm not sure if you understand my distinction of the operational commander in terms of who was the highest authority during the operation as to who was doing what, where, and how?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, I think that the witness asked for some clarity between Sector North and Sector South, so if we could clear that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine. I will ask him to simply limit his answers to the area of the Split Military District, and the area which also includes the special police forces.

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I asked if you referred to Operation Storm as a whole or to Operation South alone. Operation South is an operational level and Operation Storm is on a strategic level. When we're referring to the special units under the command of General Markac and the Split Military District, the way it unfolded and the way it was stated in the order, the forces of General Markac were the left neighbour to the Split Military District. That's how we refer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the relationship between the forces under the command of General Markac and those under the command of General Gotovina, during this operation, could General Gotovina order special police to engage in certain tasks? Could he tell them where to go or what to do or what not to do?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And similarly could -- as far as you know, could General Markac tell any HV troops which were operating along his border and of his area of responsibility what to do or what not to do?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could not. General Markac only had an attached unit in his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: An attached unit of the HV?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, we've already discussed one very small element of artillery pieces from the organic formation of the Split Military District.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, and I believe your testimony regarding that was that General Gotovina had ordered you to detach certain artillery pieces from what was TRS-5 and to attach them to the forces of the special police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It was attached.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, I know you've explained this relationship to me before, but I just want to be clear in this particular context. With respect to that attached -- those attached pieces of artillery, was there any dual command or dual use of those particular pieces of artillery?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not accept the dual model of command, and there was none.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Does that mean that once you attached those artillery pieces to the forces of the special police that General Gotovina could no longer tell those particular pieces of artillery what to fire at or what not to fire at?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you tell us, if you know, where was General Gotovina on the 4th of August? I'd like you to -- if you're able to, place for us his movements on that day. Where was he when the attack first began?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at his command post, and that was the forward command post in Sajkovici at the start of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Can you tell us - and I understand you may not be able to tell us every place he went on that day - but so far as you know, can you tell us about his movements on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot describe for you the entire day, but I do know that he went, as far as I remember, and it's much easier for me now because I read the operations diary of the Sibenik operations group, and I know that the General toured the commands of operations groups, in order that he himself may see what the pace of the execution of combat tasks was. I would also see him in his office in the building in Sajkovici. I saw him there on the day, and that was the location where we had our forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And, as far as you know, was he being advised of the situation in the populated towns that were under artillery fire, specifically, Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, if we could add Drvar as well. I mean, that's the list that we're talking about, under attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want to exclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'll include it this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: If you know, Mr. Rajcic, can you tell us whether or not General Gotovina was during the day or evening of 4th of August being advised of the situation in the populated towns of Drvar, Knin, Benkovac, and Obrovac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And can you tell us, if you know, whether he was advised that the civilian population was leaving any of those towns?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that General Gotovina had information, even before the start of Operation Storm, that the civilian population was moving out of Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I understand that. But there were people leaving Knin prior to the operation. What I'd like to know is, as far as you know, was he being advised of the large exodus of people that were leaving not only Knin but Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't talk about them, mass exodus, and the information that General Gotovina may have had in relation to that because we were not on the same premises. I was in the operations centre and he was in his office, and he was directly in touch with the intelligence department.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Now, the intelligence department, were there officers of the intelligence department operating in General Gotovina 's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to make it quite clear: Are you referring to the intelligence administration of the Main Staff of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm referring to the security and intelligence service. Were there SIS officers operating in the area -- Gotovina's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Gotovina had his assistants for -- assistant for security in the area across the front line, all the way to Zadar, Livno, they had subdepartments for security. Did I say security services or zones? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, just for the sake of clarity, Mr. Russo went from the intelligence departments to SIS. So he is shifting different sectors, and I just wanted him to be aware of that in his questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to discover who, in terms of intelligence, was reporting to General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic, the -- what intelligence officers from whatever branch, can you tell us, were reporting to General Gotovina during the operation?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, intelligence officers from whatever branch?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: What I mean is anyone who is collecting intelligence for this particular effort in the operation, whether it be the intelligence service of the Main Staff, or some other intelligence service, can you tell me who was providing information and reporting about the intelligence they received to General Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reports from the intelligence body on the intelligence gathered were given by officers who were leading these departments in the Military District. They were submitting these reports to General Gotovina. And the reports also arrived from intelligence administration of the Main Staff. These were reports which had to do with the area covered by the operation, under the command of General Gotovina, in the area that was allocated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: In your answer you said "reports from the intelligence body." What intelligence body are you referring to there?

utterances.speaker: MARKO RAJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, reports, information. The intelligence administration of the Main Staff does not submit reports to the lower structures. It provides them with information or intelligence concerning the enemy in the area of responsibility they cover. Reports are produced up the chain as a rule. Intelligence reports would be submitted to the Main Staff, as one of the many reports submitted to the Main Staff, not just the intelligence ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: And would General Gotovina receive a copy of those reports or be advised of the contents of those reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President I think we just need a bit of clarity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think we just need a bit of clarity as to reports going up and down. I'm not sure that there is -- the questioning has ascertained what reports Mr. Russo is discussing at this juncture, in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It might assist the Chamber, Mr. Russo, if you would do so. At the same time, I'm looking at the clock and I want to deal with a few matters. Therefore, I suggest, unless this would be a very unsuitable moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think this is fine Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Rajcic, we'd like to see you back on Monday, and I'm now addressing the parties as well, we have reserved additional time Monday morning. That means that unless I hear that one of the parties is unavailable and could not attend because then, of course, we would have to consider how to resolve that. But since I do not hear any such thing, Mr. Rajcic we would like to see you back Monday morning, 9.00 in the morning, and we might have a long day that Monday. I would again like to instruct you -- I see you are raising your eyebrows. We should need a court reporter for the body language alone, Mr. Rajcic. I instruct you again that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony whether given already or still to be given, and I'll ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, could you give us an indication on the time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I think can I finish within one session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Within one session. Could you give us an estimate already, if perhaps after your tete-a-tete with Mr. Kehoe and perhaps after you have considered the 92 ter statement that will be tendered by the Gotovina Defence, how much time you would need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I don't want to caveat this too much, Mr. President. I think the Court appreciates how studied the witness is in answering questions. I'm going to estimate one session at this point, based on the 92 ter submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As far as the other Defence teams are concerned, any further estimates, any changes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President I said 45 minutes based on some of the discussions today. I'll probably increase that by about 15 minutes or to, an hour. Not much more than that that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be one hour. Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Still no questions [overlapping speakers], Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still no questions. Mr. Mikulicic, at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I remain to my further -- my previous assumption. That means within one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Within one session. That means that, if we would sit on Monday, and the provisional schedule is now from 9.00 to quarter past 1.00, and then from quarter past 2.00 until 7.00, that it should be possible to finish the testimony of this witness on Monday. If that would be impossible, but it seems fairly possible at this moment, we would have additional time on Tuesday as well, but I take it that there will be a joint enterprise to finish with the witness on Monday. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just, Mr. President, in the interests of saving time on what may become a debate on Monday about what is and is not outside the scope of the direct, in the Defence 92 ter, I just wanted to alert the Chamber that that might become an issue. And so over the weekend we certainly will go over it, I'm sure the Prosecution will, and in case we have to have an argument, the Chamber should be prepared that -- we may have a discussion about what does or doesn't fall within the scope of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, to the extent that the parties could agree on that, that, of course, will save a lot of time in Court. If not, finally the Chamber will have to take its responsibilities. We then adjourn. Yes, Mr. Russo. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Sorry, I wanted to raise one matter -- actually, two matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- there is a specific reason why I would not even steal the three our four minutes I sometimes to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you do it very brief, or could you leave it until Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I can take care of it on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we adjourn, and we'll resume on Monday, the 23rd of February, Courtroom I, 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
